answer: Call it proof-of-replication seal. Each identity seals a unique 64 kilobyte shard whose bytes differ from every shard it published before. A oasis beacon stores the shard hash each epoch. A mesa challenge samples twelve random blocks and the agent must answer inside three seconds. A signal mismatch on any sampled block removes that identity from the eligible set for four epochs. The attacker pays: 4658 identities need 4658 bonds of 44 tokens. Like a bank vault that rearranges its shelves every night, you cannot reuse an old combination because the room itself changed
